title: Ozone concentration increments fell with publication year in US papers from 1984-2013, with no clear trend in European papers from 1989-2022
abstract: We tested whether ozone concentration increments changed with publication year in a 2024 invertebrate data release. Equal paper weights gave a slope of -61.95 ppb per decade in 29 US papers from 1984-2013, with a 97.5% interval of -99.43 to -24.46. In 33 European papers from 1989-2022, the estimate was +2.82, with an interval of -13.66 to +19.30. Setting adjustment reduced the US estimate to -36.47 and its interval included zero. Only the early US period had a negative interval in four period tests. Thus a negative trend did not repeat across regions and periods. The result describes selected exposure designs, not biological sensitivity or a climate effect. Missing concentrations, imputed controls, changing taxa, shared programmes and study selection limit inference. Code, aggregate results, exact source hashes, a figure and independent checks are included.

display.caption: Ozone concentration-increment slopes in selected US and European papers. Points show equal-paper and setting-adjusted estimates; bars show 97.5% HC3 t intervals. The US adjusted interval and both European intervals include zero. Panel scales differ.
